9 ارمقّ It (a skin, or hide, إِهَابٌ,) was, or became, thin. (K.) ―
-b2- Hence, said of life or the means of subsistence (العَيْشُ) [as meaning (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, narrow in its circumstances, or scanty; like رَقَّ]. (TA.) ―
-b3- It (an affair, S, or a thing, IDrd, K,) was, or became, weak; (IDrd, S, K;) and so ↓ ارماقّ said of a rope: (S, K:) or the former verb, said of a rope, it was, or became, weak in its strands. (IDrd, TA.) ―
-b4- ارمقّت الغَنَمُ The sheep, or goats, died: (IDrd, K:) and ↓ ارماقّت they (sheep, or goats,) perished, or died,
by reason of leanness, or emaciation: (Ibn- 'Abbád, TA:) or ارماقّ signifies he perished, or died, by reason thereof. (K.) ―
-b5- ارمقّ الطَّرِيقُ The road was, or became, long. (TA: but the verb is there written without the sheddeh.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
